text:
Recent work supports jointly learning recommendation and item-text representations, but provides limited direct evidence for a lightweight, from-scratch BERT4Rec text encoder. [JEPA4Rec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.10512) encodes item descriptions with a bidirectional Transformer and predicts masked sentence representations; relevant conceptual support, not a verified match to this constrained setup. [DWSRec (2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28786) combines pretrained text features with item IDs, so its reported gains do not establish effectiveness without pretrained weights. Earlier [Recformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13731) demonstrates joint text-based sequential learning but initializes from pretrained Longformer, making direct adoption unsuitable.

Practical hypothesis, rather than a literature-established result: retain BERT4Rec and add a randomly initialized token embedding table, mean-pool truncated titles/descriptions, then project and fuse with item-ID embeddings inside one jointly trained network. Start with this inexpensive encoder before attempting a text Transformer. Leakage prevention follows [BERT4Rec’s masked-target rationale](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690): replace both ID and all associated text at each supervised masked position; hiding only the ID leaves a target-identifying shortcut. At inference, append a reserved mask with no target text and read its final nonpadding position. Candidate text may enter the shared candidate-scoring representation, but never reveal the correct candidate inside sequence context. Train all components together and retain one checkpoint per category; whether this improves macro validation HR@10 remains an experimental question.
